title: Vacuole
summary: The vacuole is the cell's storage sac - a membrane bubble that holds water, salts, and materials. In plant cells a large central vacuole stores water and helps hold the plant's shape; animal cells have smaller vacuoles that also help move things.

processes: Holding plant cell shape by water pressure
plainLanguageExplanation: A vacuole is a membrane sac that stores materials. In plant cells there is usually one large central vacuole, mostly filled with water and dissolved substances, that acts like a water tank. When it is full of water, it presses against the cell wall and helps the plant stand tall; when it is empty, the plant wilts. The vacuole can also store nutrients, pigments, and waste. Animal cells have several smaller vacuoles that help store and move materials. So the vacuole is the cell's storage space and, in plants, its water support system.

whyItMatters: The vacuole is how a cell stores what it needs and, in plants, how a whole plant stands up. Understanding it explains why a plant droops when thirsty and stands tall after watering, and why storage matters to every cell.
didYouKnow: The central vacuole of a plant cell can take up most of the cell's volume - sometimes over half of its whole space.
